Status labels used in this document: VERIFIED (confirmed in the current source code or existing documents) · PROTOTYPE (works in the React/LocalStorage prototype with mock or simulated behaviour) · PROPOSED (recommended production design, not built) · PENDING CONFIRMATION (needs a client decision) · NOT IMPLEMENTED · NOT VERIFIED.

Purpose

Define what the business needs from the Bellomassi platform, independent of technology, so that the client can approve the requirement baseline for production.

Scope

Order-to-delivery process from order capture to OTP-confirmed delivery and delivery note, the Admin Panel, and the prototype extensions that need a scope decision.

Definitions

Term Definition

Prototype The React / LocalStorage application used to validate workflows; not production software

1. Executive summary

Bellomassi distributes frozen and chilled food. Orders arrive by phone, email and WhatsApp and are handled manually through approval, preparation, dispatch and delivery. The business needs one digital order path with manager approval and credit control, consolidation by Customer Service, zone-based dispatch, a driver app with the fastest route, and customer-confirmed handover by OTP with an instant delivery note, under the control of an Admin Panel and ready for SAP integration. A working prototype demonstrates these workflows today; this BRD states the business requirements for the production platform and identifies what still needs client decision.

2. Business background

See BM-OVW-006 (Project Background). The client Scope of Work (October 2026) is the requirement baseline; the Driver App GPS guide adds tracking requirements. The prototype has validated the workflows and introduced extensions (inventory, invoices, customer app, VMS, documents, communication, AI) whose production scope is not yet agreed.

3. Business objectives

OBJ-01 Control · OBJ-02 Visibility · OBJ-03 One record · OBJ-04 Efficient delivery · OBJ-05 Accountability · OBJ-06 Proof of delivery · OBJ-07 Ready for SAP — defined with proposed measures in BM-OVW-003 (Project Vision and Objectives).

4. Existing business problems

P-01 multiple channels and re-entry · P-02 manual approval and credit · P-03 unclear consolidation · P-04 manual planning, late driver information · P-05 no proof of handover · P-06 no single status · P-07 item data from emails — see BM-OVW-004 (Business Problem Statement).

5. Proposed solution

A shared platform with three applications (SOW slide 4):

  • Order Taking App (mobile and web) — capture, approve, consolidate, dispatch.
  • Drivers App (iOS and Android) — next-day plan, suggested route, OTP handover.
  • Admin Panel (web) — users, customers, items, zones, rules, live monitor, reports.

Shared services: one order record, workflow and approvals, live notifications, OTP service, maps and routing, audit trail. Second stage: SAP integration.

6. Business scope

Order capture, approval, credit check, consolidation, zone dispatch, driver app, route, OTP, delivery note, notifications, Admin Panel, reports, SAP (stage 2) Customer app, invoicing, inventory, scrap, VMS, documents / OCR, email / WhatsApp, call history, AI, extra roles Invoicing and finance documents (SOW slide 13), payments

9. Business rules

The 44 business rules enforced by the prototype are listed in BM-SYS-007 (Business Rules Catalogue). Key rules:

  1. No order is shipped without Sales Manager approval (RULE-010 … RULE-015).
  2. Credit over limit is a warning; it blocks approval when the client enables blocking (RULE-011).
  3. Every return or rejection carries a reason (RULE-014).
  4. Only approved, consolidated orders reach the Dispatcher (RULE-016, RULE-017).
  5. Only compliant, available drivers and vehicles of the right hub and capacity are assigned (RULE-023 … RULE-025).
  6. Stock leaves the hub once, at dispatch confirmation (RULE-020, RULE-021).
  7. A delivery is completed only with the customer’s valid OTP (RULE-027).
  8. Failed and partial deliveries are reviewed by the Dispatcher (RULE-031).

10. Business constraints

  • Customer messages (OTP, delivery note) require an SMS or WhatsApp provider account (SOW slide 16).
  • Maps and routing depend on a paid provider (Google Maps Platform / Routes API; usage-based charges — GPS guide §12).
  • Mobile GPS depends on drivers’ phones, permissions, battery and connectivity (GPS guide §7–8).
  • SAP integration depends on the client’s SAP interfaces (stage 2).
  • See BM-SYS-005 (System Constraints Document).

11. Assumptions

  • The SOW is the agreed functional baseline unless the client approves the extensions.
  • Drivers have company-provided or compatible smartphones with data plans.
  • Customers can receive SMS or WhatsApp messages on a registered mobile number.
  • See BM-SYS-006 (Assumptions and Dependencies).

12. Dependencies

Client master data (customers, items, zones, drivers, vehicles) · provider accounts (maps, messaging, email) · hosting decision · SAP team availability (stage 2). See BM-PM-005 (Issue, Dependency and Decision Registers).

13. Business benefits

See BM-OVW-005 (Business Benefits).

14. Success criteria — PROPOSED, pending confirmation

# Criterion
SC-01 100% of orders are captured in the platform within one month of go-live
SC-02 100% of dispatched orders have an approval record and credit check
SC-03 Drivers receive the next-day plan before the end of the previous working day
SC-04 ≥ 98% of deliveries confirmed by OTP; all exceptions reviewed within one working day
SC-05 Delivery note received by the customer within 5 minutes of handover
SC-06 Management can see the status of any order in real time

15. Acceptance criteria

The BRD is accepted when the client confirms: (1) the business requirements table, (2) the scope decision for each prototype extension (section 6), (3) the open decisions in BM-HND-012 (Pending Requirements Document). The delivered system is accepted through UAT (BM-QA-003 (User Acceptance Testing (UAT) Plan), BM-QA-012 (UAT Test Cases)).

16. Out-of-scope items

Invoicing and financial documents (unless the client brings the prototype invoice module into scope) · payments, receipts, credit notes and refunds · purchase invoices · fleet fuel and maintenance costing · cold-chain sensor hardware · driver self-registration (GPS guide §2) · dedicated truck GPS hardware (first release; GPS guide §7).

17. Risks

Key business risks (full register BM-RSK-002 (Project Risk Register)): unclear scope of extensions; country rules (UAE / India) undecided; messaging provider policy (OpenWA is unofficial); mobile GPS reliability; SAP interface availability; user adoption by drivers; data migration of customer and item master.
